Working summary (key steps)

1.  For each pipe use the Darcy–Weisbach form  
   hf = f (L/D) (V²/2g) = (8 f L Q²)/(π² g D⁵)

2.  Write the head–flow relations with the junction piezometric head HJ and assign Q positive when flow goes from a reservoir towards the junction:

   Pipe 1 (A–J): 120 – HJ = R1 Q1|Q1|  
   Pipe 2 (B–J): 100 – HJ = R2 Q2|Q2|  
   Pipe 3 (C–J):  70 – HJ = R3 Q3|Q3|

   R = 8 f L /(π² g D⁵)

3.  Impose continuity: Q1 + Q2 + Q3 = 0.

4.  Iterate:
   • assume f ≃ 0.02, obtain provisional Q’s and Re’s,  
   • evaluate f from the Colebrook relation (Swamee-Jain explicit form),  
   • update R’s and repeat until changes are negligible.

   Converged values:

   f1 = 0.0196 f2 = 0.0234 f3 = 0.0204  
   R1 = 1.00 × 10³ R2 = 4.87 × 10³ R3 = 2.07 × 10³  (SI units)

   Solving
     Q1 = +0.137 5 m³ s⁻¹
     Q2 = –0.014 9 m³ s⁻¹  (negative → flow from J to B)
     Q3 = –0.122 6 m³ s⁻¹

   gives
     HJ = 101.1 m

5.  Convert to litres per second (1 m³ s⁻¹ = 1000 L s⁻¹).

   Q1 = 137 L s⁻¹ toward J  
   |Q2| = 14.9 L s⁻¹ from J into reservoir B  
   Q3 = 123 L s⁻¹ from J toward reservoir C


FINAL (a): 101.1 m  
FINAL (b): 137 L/s  
FINAL (c): 14.9 L/s (into reservoir B)  
FINAL (d): 123 L/s
